newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus sees 96/97 refined sugar output 372,000.
newsitem.headline: Belarus sees 96/97 refined sugar output 372,000.

text.p: Belarus recently bought 260,000 tonnes of raw sugar from Brazil, which when refined will bring Belarus' 1996/97 refined sugar output to 372,000 tonnes, a top Agriculture Ministry official said Wednesday.

"We will produce 240,000 tonnes of refined sugar at our four refineries from the 260,000 tonnes," deputy director Vyacheslav Sipir told Reuters, adding that with 132,500 tonnes of whites from the 1996 beet crop Belarus could meet domestic demand.

"Up to the new year we produced 132,500 tonnes of refined sugar from the 1996 beet crop. With this and the purchase, Belarus has enough sugar for its needs and will not need to buy any more," Sipir said.
Belarus produced about 225,000 tonnes of refined sugar in the previous year -- around 132,000 tonnes from its beet harvest and 93,000 tonnes from imported raws.
The former Soviet republic's 1996 sugar beet harvest stood at 1.00 million tonnes, against 1.14 million tonnes in 1995.
